newsitem.title: UK: UK's Charter to buy Howden Group.
newsitem.headline: UK's Charter to buy Howden Group.

text.p: British engineering group Charter Plc said on Friday it agreed to buy Howden Group Plc in a recommended offer valuing the equipment maker at about 378 million pounds ($602.1 million).
The companies said the bid valued Howden shares at 128.5 pence each.
Under terms of the deal, Charter would pay 124.78 pounds in cash and three new Charter shares for every 115 Howden shares, the companies said in a joint statement.
Howden shareholders would be entitled to retain their interim dividend of 1.0 pence net per share.
The bid represented a premium of 40 percent to Howden's closing price of 91.5 pence on Thursday.
Charter, predicting the acquisition would be earnings enhancing in the first full year, said Howden had scope to improve its results through rationalisation and efficiency improvements.

"We are confident that, through our experience in growing a major industrial group with market-leading positions in its chosen sectors, Howden's business will respond to our approach to management," Charter chairman Jeffrey Herbert said.
Charter said it already had a beneficial interest in 8.75 million Howden shares, or 2.97 percent of its share capital, as a result of purchases earlier this month.
Trade in both companies' shares was temporarily suspended Friday morning ahead of the statement.
Howden's shares shot up early this week on market speculation that the company might be a takeover target.
But Howden responded on Monday by saying it had not received an approach, noting that it was in talks to dispose of an undisclosed "non-core business activity". ($ = 0.627 British Pounds)
